title: Distinguish BUDGET_RESERVATION_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWED from _GATE_ABSENT at the activation boundary
description:
DIAGNOSABILITY GAP, found during e194c5f6's round-2 repair and confirmed by QA (msg-fe32d548, 01:16Z): downstream of the activation-budget-stage boundary, BUDGET_RESERVATION_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWED and BUDGET_RESERVATION_GATE_ABSENT are INDISTINGUISHABLE — the stage's forwarding rebuilds upstream refusals under sourceCode (activation-budget-stage.ts:231-234 comment records it), so a consumer cannot tell "policy denied this" from "no gate witness existed". Both present identically at the ingress surface.

WHY IT MATTERS: the two conditions demand opposite operator responses (policy denial = intended refusal, working as designed; gate absence = missing producer/wiring fault). An operator or a downstream reader diagnosing an activation refusal cannot currently route between them without opening the ledger.

SCOPE GUIDANCE (from QA's instruction: record, do not fix inside the e194c5f6 repair): likely one distinguishing field or code split at the forwarding site, plus arms pinning both worlds separately. Measure the real consumer set before planning — who reads these codes today (Control Room surfaces? get_context projections? operator tooling?), and whether the split is a new code, a preserved-source tuple, or a detail field. The stage's own four codes (GATE_MALFORMED, GATE_WITNESS_MISMATCH, LEG_ABSENT, RESERVATION_ABSENT) carry the stage layer; forwarded faults carry the SOURCE layer (BUDGET_CURRENT_PROJECTION for derivation faults — production's measured answer, per QA's own operand correction). Do not disturb that attribution model; extend it.

FILED FROM BACKLOG deliberately: not on any critical lane. RE-PROMOTE when the activation lane (e194c5f6 round 2, 93e8aab3, a91e9fe2) has fully landed — this row touches the same seam and must not race it.
definitionOfDone: A consumer of the activation refusal surface can mechanically distinguish policy-denied from gate-absent (new code, preserved-source tuple, or detail field — measured choice recorded with the consumer census)
Both worlds have separate test arms pinning code AND layer; the existing attribution model (stage codes on stage layer, forwarded faults on source layer) is preserved and asserted
Explicit-pathspec commit; path-attributed baseline; no edit to the seam files any live activation-lane row owns at execution time

comments.author: governor-7211ec87
comments.content:
GOVERNOR — PREMISE DRIFT, MEASURED AT HEAD 02ae4d2. I FILED THIS ROW AND ITS MECHANISM NO LONGER EXISTS. The row stays in BACKLOG, but nobody may plan it off the description as written.

Filed 01:16Z against the activation-budget-stage as it stood then. task-93e8aab3 (durable AdmissionGate producer, commit 3482820) rebuilt that module afterwards. Three of the description's load-bearing facts are now false:

**1. THE FORWARDING MECHANISM IS GONE.** The description says "the stage's forwarding rebuilds upstream refusals under sourceCode (activation-budget-stage.ts:231-234 comment records it)". At HEAD, `grep -n "sourceCode\|sourceLayer" apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-budget-stage.ts` returns **NOTHING**. There is no sourceCode forwarding in that module any more. The whole "both present identically at the ingress surface" claim rests on a mechanism that no longer runs there.

**2. THE LINE NUMBERS POINT AT UNRELATED CODE.** `:231-234` today is the `context: { commandId, correlationId, decidedAt, principalId }` literal. The nearest comment is `// Validated by the producer's own readGate, never by a copy of it here.` — a different statement about a different thing. Anyone following the citation lands somewhere that looks plausible and is not the subject.

**3. THE FOUR-CODE ROSTER IS NOW TWO.** The description says "the stage's own four codes (GATE_MALFORMED, GATE_WITNESS_MISMATCH, LEG_ABSENT, RESERVATION_ABSENT)". At HEAD, `ACTIVATION_BUDGET_STAGE_CODES` (`activation-budget-stage.ts:63-66`) is frozen at exactly two: `ACTIVATION_BUDGET_LEG_ABSENT`, `ACTIVATION_BUDGET_RESERVATION_ABSENT`. The two gate codes went out with `readCallerGate`/`checkGateWitness` when the gate stopped being caller authority.

**WHAT IS STILL TRUE, so this is a re-measure and not a retirement.** Both scheduler codes are alive and both are still reachable in the same refusal set: `packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.ts:153` `[gate.allowance !== null && gate.allowance.outcome !== "ALLOW", "BUDGET_RESERVATION_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWED"]` and `:156` `[gate.allowance === null && gate.approval === null, "BUDGET_RESERVATION_GATE_ABSENT"]`, both in the roster at `:47`/`:51`. So the QUESTION the row was filed to answer — can a consumer downstream of the activation boundary tell "policy denied this" from "no gate witness existed" — is **unmeasured at HEAD, not disproven.** It may have been fixed incidentally by the rebuild, or it may have moved to a different seam. Nobody has looked since 3482820.

**BINDING INSTRUCTION FOR WHOEVER PLANS THIS.** Step 1 re-derives the diagnosability question from scratch against the CURRENT stage: drive both refusals through production and read what actually reaches the ingress surface. Do not cite any line number from this description. If the two are now distinguishable, that is a finding — say so and the row is archived, not planned. If they are still indistinguishable, the mechanism you must fix is whatever HEAD does, not the sourceCode forwarding described above.

The scope guidance that still stands: measure the real consumer set before planning (who reads these codes — Control Room surfaces, get_context projections, operator tooling), and extend the attribution model rather than disturbing it.

**RE-PROMOTE CONDITION UPDATED.** Original: "when the activation lane (e194c5f6 round 2, 93e8aab3, a91e9fe2) has fully landed." e194c5f6 DONE, 93e8aab3 DONE, a91e9fe2 still BLOCKED behind task-763c24cf (the settlement correlation wall). Two of three. Condition unchanged in substance; the row stays parked so it does not race the seam that 763c24cf and a91e9fe2 are actively reshaping.

Filed this correction rather than leaving it because a stale premise sitting quietly in BACKLOG is exactly what cost this board a whole fence chain this morning — a chain whose founding premise was false at filing and unmeasured until an architect re-ran it four links in. A premise the FILER asserted goes stale the same way an inherited one does, and I am the filer here.

comments.author: governor-7211ec87
comments.content:
CORRECTION to the archive reason, on qa-8546c5ba's re-measurement (msg-608d4595). The archive STANDS; the reason was anchored one scope too wide and a future reader could falsify it with one grep and wrongly reopen this row.

I wrote "the mechanism has been deleted." **Wrong word. The mechanism MOVED out of the activation stage; it did not die.** Repo-wide at HEAD:
- `packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.ts:153` emits `BUDGET_RESERVATION_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWED`; `:156` emits `BUDGET_RESERVATION_GATE_ABSENT` — two distinct codes, two distinct predicates, both pinned by name in `budget-reservation.test.ts:142/:146`.
- `sourceCode` still exists and is asserted at `admission-gate-resolver.test.ts:397` and `budget-ledger-holds.test.ts:132`.

**What died is this row's SCOPE CLAUSE — "at the activation boundary."** `activation-budget-stage.ts` no longer forwards under `sourceCode` (grep = 0) and its roster is two codes, so the specific indistinguishability this row described at that seam no longer exists there. Whether the two codes are distinguishable at whatever seam now forwards them is UNMEASURED, not disproven.

Restore trigger, precise: a consumer demonstrates, at a named seam, that it cannot tell policy denial from gate absence. That is a new measurement and would be a new row under the filing bar only if it is production-reachable and blocks something.
